title: Vitamin D and Omega-3 Trial - American College of Cardiology
abstract: The VITAL trial showed that supplementation with either n–3 fatty acid at a dose of 1 g/day or vitamin D3 at a dose of 2000 IU/day was not effective for primary prevention of CV or cancer events among healthy middle-aged men and women over 5 years of follow-up. The goal of the trial was to assess the cardiovascular (CV) and cancer benefits of n–3 (also called omega-3) fatty acid and vitamin D3 supplementation compared with placebo among healthy participants. The results of this trial indicate that supplementation with either n–3 fatty acid at a dose of 1 g/day or vitamin D3 at a dose of 2000 IU/day was not effective for primary prevention of CV or cancer events among healthy middle-aged men and women over 5 years of follow-up. **Keywords:** *AHA Annual Scientific Sessions,* *AHA18,* *Cholecalciferol,* *Coronary Disease,* *Docosahexaenoic Acids,* *Eicosapentaenoic Acid,* *Fatty Acids, Omega-3,* *Fish Oils,* *Middle Aged,* *Myocardial Infarction,* *Neoplasms,* *Primary Prevention,* *Stroke,* *Vitamin D,* *Diabetes Mellitus, Type 2*.
